There is no partial credit; the\n10\t        f2p_passed / p2p_passed counts carry how close a run got.\n11\t\n12\tf2p (fail-to-pass): tests that FAIL on base, PASS after fix. Three defects are covered, all within\n13\t    \"the follow experience\" but only one disclosed by mechanism in instruction.md (the closing line\n14\t    tells the agent there is more than one, without saying what or where) - see task.toml's\n15\t    difficulty_explanation:\n16\t      - the FollowingIndicator slot renders inside the UI layout's own stacking context\n17\t        (.tlui-layout), after the panel groups, instead of inside the canvas's lower-stacking-\n18\t        context overlay (.tl-canvas__in-front) where panels always painted over it - including the\n19\t        focus-mode branch, which swaps out the panel chrome but must not swap out the follow\n20\t        border along with it (disclosed, image-gated);\n21\t      - the camera-follow viewport-fit math in Editor.ts correctly grows to contain the followed\n22\t        user's viewport across mismatched aspect ratios (undisclosed by mechanism);\n23\t      - the page-follow effect in the same Editor.ts method switches the follower's page when the\n24\t        leader actually navigates elsewhere, instead of only when their page already matches ours\n25\t        (undisclosed by mechanism).\n26\tp2p (pass-to-pass): tests that PASS on both base and fix. These guard against regressions to the\n27\t    sibling in-front-of-canvas slots (rich text/image/video toolbars, cursor chat bubble) that the\n28\t    disclosed fix's diff also touches, and against the fix accidentally rendering the indicator when\n29\t    nobody is being followed or rendering it more than once.\n30\t\n31\tBEHAVIORAL CONTRACT: reward is derived entirely from the test report.\n32\tThis verifier NEVER inspects source code for the fix string or any other token.\n33\t\"\"\"\n34\timport json, os, re, sys, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET\n35\t\n36\tCONF       = json.load(open('/tests/config.json'))\n37\tF2P        = CONF['f2p']\n38\tP2P        = CONF['p2p']\n39\tREPORT     = '/logs/verifier/report.xml'\n40\t\n41\t\n42\t# ── Canonical reward writer + --rubric gate ──────────────────────────────────\n43\t# reward.json MUST be a FLAT map of numbers with exactly these seven keys: harbor parses\n44\t# it as VerifierResult.rewards and PREFERS it over reward.txt. A nested dict, list or\n45\t# string raises a ValidationError that aborts the trial before any reward is recorded —\n46\t# while reward.txt still gets written in-container, so the run looks scored when harbor\n47\t# stored nothing. Registered with atexit so it writes last.\n48\timport atexit\n49\t\n50\t_CANON_JSON = '/logs/verifier/reward.json'\n51\t_CANON_TXT  = '/logs/verifier/reward.txt'\n52\t_canon = {}\n53\t\n54\t\n55\tdef canon_reward(f2p_passed, f2p_total, p2p_passed, p2p_total, rubric):\n56\t    \"\"\"THE reward policy. BINARY — there is no partial credit.\n57\t\n58\t    tests_passed is 1.0 only when every f2p test passes AND every p2p test still passes.\n59\t    A strict subset of f2p passing is not partial progress worth scoring: the task is\n60\t    unsolved, so it is 0.0. A \"pass\" or \"not graded\" rubric verdict never lowers the score.\n61\t    \"\"\"\n62\t    f, t = int(f2p_passed), int(f2p_total)\n63\t    p, q = int(p2p_passed), int(p2p_total)\n64\t    solved = bool(t) and f == t and p == q\n65\t    tests_passed = 1.0 if solved else 0.0\n66\t    _canon.clear()\n67\t    _canon.update({\n68\t        'reward': 0.0 if rubric == 'fail' else tests_passed,\n69\t        'tests_passed': tests_passed,\n70\t        'f2p_passed': f, 'f2p_total': t,\n71\t        'p2p_passed': p, 'p2p_total': q,\n72\t        'rubric_passed': {'pass': 1, 'fail': 0}.get(rubric, -1),\n73\t    })\n74\t    return _canon['reward']\n75\t\n76\t\n77\t@atexit.register\n78\tdef _canon_flush():\n79\t    if not _canon:\n80\t        return\n81\t    try:\n82\t        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(_CANON_JSON), exist_ok=True)\n83\t        with open(_CANON_JSON, 'w') as fh:\n84\t            json.dump(_canon, fh, indent=2)\n85\t        # reward.txt too: harbor prefers reward.json, but the sandbox teardown script and\n86\t        # the lighthouse UI read reward.txt. One dict writes both, so they cannot disagree.\n87\t        with open(_CANON_TXT, 'w') as fh:\n88\t            fh.write(str(_canon['reward']))\n89\t    except Exception as exc:\n90\t        print(f\"WARNING: could not write {_CANON_JSON}: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n91\t\n92\t\n93\tdef rubric_verdict(argv):\n94\t    \"\"\"The verdict test.sh hands in as `--rubric pass|fail|\"\"`.\n95\t\n96\t    Anything that is not an explicit pass/fail — including the empty string test.sh passes\n97\t    when no rubric shipped — means \"not graded\", which must never penalise the run.\n98\t    \"\"\"\n99\t    if '--rubric' not in argv:\n100\t        return None\n101\t    i = argv.index('--rubric')\n102\t    value = argv[i + 1].strip().lower() if i + 1 < len(argv) else ''\n103\t    return value if value in ('pass', 'fail') else None\n104\t\n105\t\n106\t\n107\tdef load_results():\n108\t    \"\"\"Return {combined_id: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'} from the JUnit XML.\"\"\"\n109\t    results = {}\n110\t    if not os.path.exists(REPORT):\n111\t        return results\n112\t    try:\n113\t        tree = ET.parse(REPORT)\n114\t    except ET.ParseError as exc:\n115\t        print(f\"[verifier] WARNING: could not parse {REPORT}: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n116\t        return results\n117\t    for tc in tree.iter('testcase'):\n118\t        #
